## Trailing edge holder

The wing root is driven by the gears and sweeps through the full **60°** set in
[Module 5](05-frame-crank.qmd). The trailing edge is not driven. It is anchored
to the **tail tube**, and that anchor is what makes the membrane twist as the
wing sweeps. It sets the angle of attack the wing sees through the stroke.
Move it and the wing behaves differently. So this part is a trim adjustment as
much as it is a mount, which is why both its positions have to stay changeable
after the robot is built.

This part is a design exercise. The requirements are fixed; the mechanism is not.

| Requirement | Why |
|---|---|
| Rotates with the wing through the whole stroke | The root swings 34° up and 26° down. An anchor that cannot follow loads the membrane in the one direction it cannot take. |
| Adjustable **longitudinally**, along the tube | Fore/aft position sets wing twist. This is the trim actually reached for in [Module 11](11-wet-testing.qmd). |
| Each Wing mounts can change **laterally and longitudinally** | Sets how far the anchor stands off the boom, and is how left and right are matched. |
| Wing comes off without dismantling anything | Wings get swapped, damaged and rebuilt. Nothing about this joint may be permanent. |
| Survives repeated wet cycling | To not fail at competition |

: What the trailing edge holder has to do {#tbl-te-requirements}

### Find a solution
Both flexible and rigid solutions are possible. For a rigid solution, the mount half is straightforward: a **split collar** that slides along the
5 mm tube and clamps with an M2 screw into a square half nut, per the house
convention in [Design notes](/reference/design-notes.qmd). Sliding it gives the
longitudinal adjustment, rotating it about the tube gives some of the lateral,
and a slotted arm gives the rest.

The design must be justified against @tbl-te-requirements, and the choices defended.

### Print it

1.  3D-print the part with the material required.

### Insert it on the tube

Slide the collar onto the tail tube and set it to the starting station.
Measure from a fixed datum, write the number down, and set the second one
to the same number. 

### Attach the wing

Connect each wing's trailing edge to its holder.


::: {.callout-warning}
## Both sides must be set identically

Different longitudinal stations left and right means different twist left and
right, which is a roll bias -the same failure mode as mismatched wings in
[Module 7](07-wings.qmd), arriving by a different route and just as hard to
trim out in [Module 11](11-wet-testing.qmd).
:::
